newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB sees continued growth in profits.
newsitem.headline: UCB sees continued growth in profits.

text.p: Belgian chemicals, drugs and films group UCB said on Tuesday it expected ordinary profits to continue to grow in 1997, noting prospects remained very favourable in its three sectors.
Ordinary pre-tax profits grew by 33 percent in 1996 to 5.6 billion francs.

UCB chief executive officer Georges Jacobs told Tuesday's annual general meeting that drugs sales were increasing in almost all markets, reflecting the strength of anti-allergy drug Zyrtec, which continued to penetrate the American market. The other specialty drugs also continued to make progress.
In chemicals demand remained firm. The company was implementing various expansion projects in Asia.
Jacobs said UCB would invest almost 9.2 billion francs this year, with 5.2 billion going to research and development.
He reiterated that the group would book a surplus of the order of one billion francs in 1997 following a share sale by one of its subsidiaries.
Societe Financiere UCB SA sold 3.7 percent in Financiere d'Obourg to holding company Financiere de Tubize, increasing Tubize's stake in Obourg to 63.5 percent.
Obourg holds an exact 36.9 percent in UCB.
Tubize is controlled by Belgium's Janssen family, founders of Belgian chemicals group Solvay, which it also controls via holding company Solvac.
UCB is paying out 32 percent of profits in 1996, or a net dividend of 750 francs per share against 600 last year. Payment of the final 650 franc dividend is due on June 25.
The remainder would be added to reserves, raising own funds to 26 billion at end-1996 from 22 billion at end-1995.
